text.p: England coach David Lloyd was censured on Sunday by the Test and County Cricket Board (TCCB) over his behaviour at the end of the first test against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo.

Lloyd was originally spoken to by ICC (International Cricket Council) match referee Hanumant Singh after he was seen making obscene gestures to members of the Zimbabwe Cricket Union (ZCU) during the closing stages of the test.
He also had a public argument with a ZCU official about the tactics which Zimbabwe employed to ensure a draw.
TCCB chief executive Tim Lamb, speaking in Harare, said that Lloyd had been warned over his future conduct. He would not give details.
"The matter has been noted and recorded and I would not want to see any repeat," he said.
"Of course it is a concern if one of the members of the England management is the subject of an inquiry by the match referee.
"The appropriate action has been taken and we consider the matter to be closed."

Lloyd received a vote of confidence, however, from former England cricketer Ian Botham who denied reports in a British Sunday newspaper that he was on the verge of quitting his post of technical advisor to the England squad.
"Some of the quotes are correct, but they are things I have said over a period of time," Botham said in a television interview.
"For instance I believe in putting one man in charge of selection and it's no secret that I would do the job for a fee of 150,000 pounds ($250,000) a year.
"But I don't have a problem with Bumble (David Lloyd) or the team. We've had a laugh about it (the article)."
Lloyd was also quick to play down the newspaper article which claimed that Botham wanted a greater say in team selection.

"We don't have a problem," he said. "Ian's working well with the team, especially the bowlers. We've only just got together and I'm sure we'll go from strength to strength." ($ = 0.590 British Pounds)
